newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST - Australian General News - June 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Australian General News - June 11.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

The Reserve Bank of Australia yesterday announced changes to the prime assets requirement, an important regulatory measure, that could see the release of A$12 billion in funds for Australian banks. The RBA said it was reducing from 6 to 3 per cent the poportion of liabilities against which banks have to hold assets in the form of balances held at the Reserve Bank, Commonwealth bonds and notes and coins. Page 1.

The Australian Stock Exchange is set to expand into the Internet market, establishing the Alternative Capital Market within the next three months. The move is designed to be a more effective way of raising small equity amounts. Page 1.

A senior adviser to Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto has informed Prime Minister John Howard that Japan's support for Australian attempts to establish closer relations with Asia has been put in doubt by the Federal Government's handling of human ights issues and Asian immigration. Observers interpret this development as an unprecedented attempt by Japan to impose conditions on its political support for Australia in international contexts. Page 1.

A report by investment bank HSBC James Capel has predicted the Australian economy will enter a downturn following the Sydney 2000 Olympic Games. In the four years prior to the event Australia, as the host country, will enjoy an average economic growth of 1.3 per centage points above the long-term trends, but this will be succeeded by avaverage 0.8 point decline in private consumption and employment growth after the event. Page 5.
THE AUSTRALIAN

The Federal Government was buoyed yesterday by an Australian Chamber of Commerce and Industry-Westpac Bank survey of industry trends which showed that confidence in the manufacturing sector in the last June quarter rose to its highest level in two-and-a-half years. The change of attitude apparently followed the May Budget and the recent cuts in official interest rates. Page 1.

Champion golfer Australian Greg Norman has placed an order for a A$40 million Boeing 737, designed especially for business use. Boeing executives confirmed yesterday that Norman would pay the standard price of A$39.5 mullion for the aeroplane, despite having signed a seven-year, multi-million dollar "ambassador" sponsorship deal with the company. Page 1.

Federal Health Minister Michael Wooldridge has pledged Federal support for the investigation ordered yesterday by the Victorian Government into allegations that babies and small children in Victoria were used as secret guinea-pigs in medical research and experments in the period between World War II and 1970.

SA Premier John Olsen has been named as the source of the Cabinet leaks to the Opposition that were instrumental in deposing former State Premier Dean Brown. State Opposition leader Mike Rann made the allegations at a hearing of a federal parliamentary inquiry into the National Crime Authority.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Article highlights the widespread problem of drug abuse in Sydney with a report on how 58 used needles were gathered by police from Kings Cross in one hour. Some of these would have been distributed by the NSW Health Department under its needle exchange programme, but the majority are not exchanged needles and cannot be traced. Page 1.

Federal Cabinet yesterday confirmed the introduction of a single youth allowance which will combine Austudy and unemployment benefits, and extend the Austudy parent income test to unemployed 18-20 year olds who live at home. The new measure is aimed at encouraging young people out of the workforce and into full -time study. Page 2.

The NSW Government will not makeup the A$40 million funding shortfall which is jeopardising the staging of the Sydney 2000 Paralympics Games. This is despite the public support given by Premier Bob Carr to the event when he stated the Paralympics were as important as any other part of the Olympic Games. Page 3.

The NSW Government has re-affirmed its support for the State's banking hotline for customer inquiries, refusing a request by Commonwealth Bank managing director David Murray for it to be abolished. Murray claims the hotline only incites public hostility towards banks. Page 3.
THE AGE

A vaccine, jointly developed by researchers at the Ludwig Oncology Unit at the Austin Hospital and scientists from Belgium and Germany, is being hailed as an effective new treatment for melanoma skin cancer. In recent trials held in Australia the vaccine stopped or reversed the progress of melanoma in over 50 per cent of patients with advanced forms of the disease. Page 1.

Long-term champion football player Gary Ablett has been scheduled for serious knee surgery, casting doubts on his future viability as a player. Ablett's contract with Geelong expires at the end of the current season and is not likely to be renewed due to his age and knee injury. Page A1.

The Environment Protection Authority study has approved plans to build two exhaust towers above Melbourne's city link tunnels. The decision has provoked angry criticism from Green groups and inner suburban residents. Page A2.

An Australian Bureau of Statistics study has revealed almost six million Australians over the age of 15 participate in an organised sport each year. Aerobics is the most popular activity, followed by golf, tennis, netball, lawn bowls, swimming, basketbal, martial arts , cricket and tenpin bowling. Page A3.
